correctness.rationale: For positive a_i,b_i, isolate any two leaf generators using Kumar--Saha's generator-deletion proposition for componentwise linear ideals. With u=x^a y^b of degree d<=f=deg(v=z^c y^e), the new degree-f slice is u*m^(f-d)+(v). Its overlap with (v) is the principal ideal (v*x^a*y^max(b-e,0)) with generating degree f+a+max(b-e,0). The linear-resolution exact sequence requires f+1, hence exactly a=1,b<=e (and for equal degrees both leaf exponents must be 1 and center exponents equal). These pair inequalities imply at most one heavy leaf a_e>1 and b_e>=b_i for all others. Conversely, order unit-leaf generators by increasing b_i and append the exceptional generator. Every earlier quotient u_i/gcd(u_i,u_j)=x_i, so all colons are generated by variables in nondecreasing total degree, proving componentwise linearity over every field. s=1 is principal and included. The exact syzygy calculation, not the finite verification log, establishes the universal theorem.

originality.rationale: The complete new mathematical statement is an arbitrary-edge-exponent star characterization of componentwise linearity, plus equivalence to increasing-degree linear quotients. Published Kumar--Saha (2026) prove the co-chordal necessary condition and classify *single linear resolutions*, requiring common center exponents in their equigenerated minimal star regime. Kumar--Nanduri--Saha and Hibi--Seyed Fakhari cover vertex-consistent weighted ideals, not independent b_i per incident edge. These are logical distinctions, not just different titles. Full-text comparison finds no dominating theorem covering all edge-exponent assignments. Assessment is best-of-knowledge, not priority certification.
